# wso2is_email_sender (Resource)

Manages the tenant's email provider. In the Console, this is **Notification Channels > Email Provider**. The server uses it to send verification, account recovery, one-time password and notification emails. Each tenant has one email provider.

This resource does not work in the super tenant (`carbon.super`). The super tenant reads its email provider only from `deployment.toml` (`[output_adapter.email]`), and the API answers HTTP 405. Use this resource with a provider that manages another tenant. To import, use the ID `EmailPublisher`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Not available in the super tenant (carbon.super): configure [output_adapter.email]
# in deployment.toml there. Use a provider configured for another tenant.
provider "wso2is" {
  alias         = "acme"
  tenant_domain = "acme.com"
  username      = "admin@acme.com"
  password      = var.acme_admin_password
}

resource "wso2is_email_sender" "smtp" {
  provider     = wso2is.acme
  smtp_host    = "smtp.sendgrid.net"
  smtp_port    = 587
  from_address = "no-reply@acme.com"
  display_name = "Acme"
  reply_to     = "support@acme.com"
  username     = "apikey"
  password     = var.smtp_password
  properties = {
    "mail.smtp.starttls.enable" = "true"
  }
}

variable "acme_admin_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}

variable "smtp_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `from_address` (String) Sender address.

### Optional

- `auth_type` (String) How the server signs in to the email provider. `BASIC` is the default and uses `username` and `password`. `CLIENT_CREDENTIAL` uses the `clientId`, `clientSecret`, `tokenEndpoint` and `scopes` properties. `BEARER` uses `accessToken`. `API_KEY` is for HTTP providers. `NONE` sends no credentials.
- `display_name` (String) Sender name shown to recipients (`mail.smtp.signature`). SMTP providers need this value.
- `password` (String, Sensitive) Password for `BASIC` authentication. The server never returns this value.
- `properties` (Map of String) Additional properties, for example `mail.smtp.starttls.enable`, `mail.smtp.auth`, or for HTTP providers `body`, `http.client.method`, `contentType`, `http.headers`. Only the keys listed are managed.
- `provider_type` (String) The kind of email provider. `SMTP` is the default. With `HTTP` (WSO2 IS 7.3 and later), the server posts each email to `provider_url`.
- `provider_url` (String) Endpoint of an HTTP email provider. Set the request template in `properties.body`.
- `reply_to` (String) Reply-to address (`mail.smtp.replyTo`). SMTP providers need this value.
- `secret_properties` (Map of String, Sensitive) Confidential properties such as `clientSecret` or `accessToken`. The server never returns this value.
- `smtp_host` (String) SMTP server host (SMTP providers).
- `smtp_port` (Number) SMTP server port, for example `587`.
- `username` (String) Username for `BASIC` authentication.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `EmailPublisher`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import wso2is_email_sender.smtp EmailPublisher
```
